headline: A strong cold front brings heavy rain, damaging wind, and dangerous surf tonight into Sunday morning, with more wet weather next week.
summary: As of Saturday afternoon, a strong cold front crosses western Washington from this evening into Sunday morning. Expect widespread lowland rain, gusty south winds, and mountain snow at higher elevations. Winds are the main concern overnight. A High Wind Warning is in effect for the coast, where forecasters give a 50-70% chance of gusts over 55 mph. A Wind Advisory covers interior lowlands including Seattle, where gusts of 45 to 50 mph are expected at times. Many trees still have leaves, so localized power outages are possible, and heavy rain could clog storm drains this evening. Waves of 22 to 28 feet are expected on the beaches tonight under a High Surf Warning, which makes the razor clam dig dangerous. There is a 20-30% chance of isolated thunderstorms, mainly on the coast, and a 10-20% chance inland, where a lightning strike or two is possible. Winds peak overnight into early Sunday morning and ease steadily by late Sunday afternoon. On Sunday the steady rain turns to showers, mostly over the North Cascades and Olympics. The snow level (the elevation where rain turns to snow) falls from around 7000-7500 feet to 4500 feet, and highs are in the mid 50s. After a break Sunday evening, another system brings widespread rain and locally breezy conditions Monday, with the most rain over the Olympics. Wet, breezy, warmer weather continues Tuesday into Wednesday, with more systems expected late in the week. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will saturate soils and raise river flows, which could become a concern with storms late next week. Forecasters call the computer model guidance for next week "a bit shaky" on timing and strength, though an active pattern looks likely.
changes: The afternoon update added a 20-30% chance of coastal thunderstorms (10-20% inland) and a 50-70% chance of coastal gusts over 55 mph, and raised the forecast wave heights to 22 to 28 feet from 22 to 26. It also added details on Sunday's snow level drop. Forecasters grew more cautious about next week, calling model guidance "a bit shaky," and the morning mention of near-record warmth Wednesday was not repeated.
